header: The inputs and the formula, and no total
lead: One row per thing that is counted, the rate that applies to it, and a line on how to count it. The formula is written out underneath in rich text.
bodytext:
Total = base + (quantity × rate) + extras

The formula belongs in the rich text, where an editor can set a worked example beside it. The element does no arithmetic of its own: a figure it produced would be a quotation nobody at the company had seen.
note: The note says which rates apply and what overrides them — a written offer usually does.

inputs.title: What is counted is the row header
inputs.text: So a rate read on its own still knows what it applies to.

inputs.title: The rate keeps its own column
inputs.text: Tabular figures, so the amounts line up down the sheet.

inputs.title: How to count it is the third column
inputs.text: Where the reader finds the number to multiply — last month's invoice, a statistics page, a headcount.

inputs.title: A range is a legitimate rate
inputs.text: Not everything a sheet counts has one price.
